findings.text: The node claim has no staleness or liveness reclamation. _claim_node_dispatch (:1655) raises on FileExistsError unconditionally, and _read_node_dispatch_claim (:1605) reads the holder record for naming only: nothing checks whether the holder's pid is alive or whether created_at is older than any bound, and nothing else in the repository removes a file under NODE_DISPATCH_CLAIM_DIRECTORY. A dispatcher killed between the exclusive create (os.open at :1673) and the finally release (:7106) therefore leaves a claim that refuses every later dispatch of that (project, worktree identity, node) permanently, naming a dead pid. Reproduced in a scratch tree: writing a claim record {run_id: r-dead, pid: 999999} for (proj, sess, node-x) then calling _claim_node_dispatch raises CrewError "a dispatch of node 'node-x' ... is already in flight as run 'r-dead', pid 999999 since 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z; its claim is ..." though no such process can exist, and the file is still present after the refusal. This is the shape the live-pointer launch claim explicitly avoids -- _publish_launch_claim reasons about 'a run whose process has not started yet rather than a run whose process has died' -- and the repo's standing rule that a stale hold is self-sustaining until something clears it. The claim's life is one dispatch() call, so the window is small, but the wedge is total for the node until an operator removes the file by hand. Fix: on FileExistsError, treat a holder whose pid is not alive (or whose created_at exceeds a named bound) as reclaimable and take the claim by unlink-then-create, recording the reclaim; alternatively have the refusal name the cleanup command.
